zoom_levels_observed: B: punch-in on the stream's chat overlay, ~2-3x tighter than A (locked)
framing_style.description: DIGITAL reframing of a single static-camera stream, and completely frame-locked - there is no ramp at all. Brute-force scale+phase-correlation alignment of a background mask (couch, wall, TV) against a reference frame gives s=1.0000 with |dx|,|dy| < 0.4 px at every sampled main-shot frame from t=0.000 to t=17.100 (two samples read 1.0040, which is one 0.004 quantisation step and shows no trend). Scale ramp = 0.00 %/s. The chat punch-in shot (2.950-6.050) is independently locked too: s in 0.996-1.004, sub-pixel dx/dy, no monotonic drift. Digital rather than physical: zero rotation, zero scale drift inside either shot, the room furniture is pixel-static for whole seconds at a time (couch-patch inter-frame MAD median 0.00066, wall-patch 0.00007), and shot B is visibly soft blown-up footage sitting under crisp vector captions. Only two crop windows are ever used and both are fixed, so the whole clip is reproducible as two static crop rectangles on one source.

caption.position: centred horizontally (text bbox centre x = 540/1080, exactly frame centre); text bbox centre y = 1412/1920 = 73.5% of frame height; the black card spans 69.4%-78.5% of frame height
caption.style_description: Heavy condensed sans (Impact/Anton-like), ALL CAPS, ~111 px cap height (5.8% of frame height), sitting on an OPAQUE BLACK rounded-corner card that is auto-sized to the text with even padding. 40 cards in 17.1 s; captions are on screen 991/1028 frames (96.4%). Cards are 1-3 words, usually 1-2. Speech is transcribed verbatim including hesitations, with trailing hyphens on interrupted words (SO-, BEN DA DON-, I DONT WANT-). Non-speech action beats are written as red asterisk annotations (*LOOKS AT CHAT*, *CHAT SPAMMING AD*).
caption.color: #FFFFFF white for spoken words (measured 251,251,251). #FF0000 pure red for asterisk action annotations (measured 241,4,3 / 234,6,5). Red is used only from 2.20 s to 6.05 s; every other card is white. No frame ever mixes the two colours.
caption.outline: None. There is no stroke and no drop shadow - legibility comes entirely from a solid opaque black card behind the text (measured max channel < 28 over the whole card).
caption.animation: Centre-anchored uniform scale pop on every card, box and text scaling together, measured on 8 separate card starts and identical each time: start scale 0.909 (range 0.907-0.912) at the card's first frame, growing monotonically to a peak of 1.050 (range 1.047-1.055) at frame +5 = +83 ms, then relaxing back and settling at exactly 1.000 by frame +8 = +133 ms. NO undershoot - it approaches 1.0 from above and stops. Per CARD, not per word: bbox width and height scale by the same factor while bbox centre x stays pinned at 270.0 (frame centre) and centre y at 76.0, so it is one uniform scale about the card centre, not a per-word reveal (which would grow width only) and not a full-frame composite ramp (the rest of the frame is unaffected at those frames).

effects: no editor-added effects at all: no zoom lines, no flash frames, no added emoji or stickers, no meme cutaways, no arrows or circles, no border, no grain, no vignette, no chromatic aberration, no progress bar, no speed ramp

source-native Twitch alert overlays are burned into the stream and pass through: a red NEW SUBSCRIBER banner (6.05-7.5 s, fades out on its own) and an animated gift-box 'has gifted subs to viewers!' alert (9.88-12.75 s)
the stream's own chat overlay, visible only in the punch-in shot B (2.95-6.05 s)
hook: No visual hook device whatsoever - no title card, no zoom, no flash, no sound effect. It opens cold and mid-sentence on the locked medium-close framing, first caption 'SO-' already up at t=0.05 s, then a tight jump cut at 0.65 s straight into 'BEN DA DON-' (a name). The hook is purely verbal: drop the viewer into a story already in progress, name a person, and use a sub-second first shot so the pace reads as urgent. The first cut at 0.65 s is the shortest shot in the clip.
audio: Raw source audio only - no music bed, no sfx on cuts, no mastering. Integrated -23.4 LUFS (very quiet; quieter than every sibling measured so far), LRA 7.2 LU, true peak -9.1 dBFS, so ~14 dB of unused headroom. Opus 48 kHz stereo 114 kb/s; L/R correlation 0.98, i.e. effectively mono mic. A music bed is ruled out by a genuine near-silent gap at 14.40-14.55 s that falls to -47.9 dB RMS with -107 dB above 2 kHz and -128 dB above 6 kHz - a bed would hold the floor up. 150 ms RMS runs from -30.8 dB (p1) to -19.3 dB (p99), consistent with one unprocessed speaking voice. The silence gap sits exactly on the 14.517 s cut, which independently confirms that edit point.
notes:
NOT near-uncut. The prior mechanical pass (~3.5 cuts/min, one cut) was wrong by about 9x; the verified figure is 9 cuts / 31.5 cuts per minute. Threshold counts on caption-masked per-frame MAD: 2 hits at 0.10 (2.950, 6.050), 0 at 0.20, 0 at 0.35 - so a threshold-only method finds only the two obvious reframes and misses all seven jump cuts, which is exactly the failure mode warned about. Caption band was located by a full-height row scan (temporal change + horizontal gradient) at 70.4-77.1% of frame height, peak 72.9% - well below the sibling cluster - and masked out before differencing. Motion baseline is low so local-median normalisation was computed but not needed to separate hits.

HOW THE LIST WAS BUILT. Candidates came from masked MAD plus a local-median-normalised version, then each was judged on five independent channels: (1) spike isolation r1 = d(n-1,n) / max(d(n-2,n-1), d(n,n+1)); (2) subject-pose continuity, stepped frame by frame at 60 fps on a head crop; (3) MAD on static furniture the subject never touches (couch patch, wall patch), whose within-shot medians are 0.00066 and 0.00007 - essentially frozen; (4) the TV screen, which the subject cannot occlude; (5) the source's own overlay animations used as clocks. Every one of the 9 accepted cuts shows a one-frame discontinuity in static furniture with the framing provably locked, and 7 of them also show a visible subject-pose jump at full frame rate. 2.950 and 6.050 are unambiguous full reframes (couch patch x288 and x276, wall patch x2162 and x2169 over local median) and 2.950 also forced an encoder I-frame. 14.517 is confirmed three ways: couch x199, TV x95, and a 167 ms audio silence gap straddling it.

REJECTED CANDIDATES. Four moments scored high but are not cuts. 7.400 s is the closest call and I rejected it: static-furniture and TV both spike, but the subject is provably continuous across it (he is motionless with his head down, and frames 441-447 step smoothly), r1 is only 2.17 because 442-443 are also elevated - a plateau, not an isolated spike - and the couch patch's high-frequency energy jumps 1.54x at exactly that frame, which is an AV1 quality-refresh signature that the 7 accepted jump cuts do not show (they sit at 0.98-1.13x). 2.633, 10.550, 12.317, 12.933 and 16.650 were surfaced by a systematic isolated-spike scan over the static regions and all were rejected on inspection: the couch pattern does not change structure, it only becomes crisper, and for 10.550 and 12.317 the gift-box alert animation - an independent clock running through 9.9-12.75 s - is continuous to 0.15 and 0.45 px against a 43.7 px step at the confirmed 12.750 cut. This is the mirror image of the sibling warning: here the codec fires where there is no cut.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY. 11.717 is accepted but is the weakest of the nine: the head jump is small, the gift-box clock steps only 0.24 px (about 8 frames of removed time, so a very tight trim), and its supporting evidence is a one-frame appearance of his shoulder in the couch patch plus an encoder I-frame placed one frame later at 11.733. 6.700 is similar but stronger (r1 = 10.0, couch x11, TV x12). If either is spurious the count drops to 8 and cuts/min to 28.0.

OTHER. Not 30-in-60: mpdecimate keeps 1010 of 1028 frames (98.2%), so the 60 fps is real, not duplicated 30 fps. All 9 cuts are same-scene - 2 reframe between the two fixed crop windows, 7 are jump cuts on the identical framing that simply remove time - so same_scene_reframe_pct is 100 and nothing cuts to separately-filmed footage. Nothing in the clip needs background removal, a composite, or an extra filtergraph input; a single-source renderer reproduces all of it with two static crop rectangles, a cut list, and the caption layer. The one figure I could not pin down is the exact zoom ratio of punch-in shot B relative to shot A: the two crops show different parts of the couch so they cannot be directly registered, and a texture-autocorrelation estimate only brackets it at roughly 2-3x, so 'about 2-3x tighter' is stated rather than a single number. words_per_card = 1.6 is from counting 45 words across the 29 cards legible in the sheets, not all 40 detected cards. Speaker-colour test is NOT APPLICABLE: there is exactly one person on screen and one voice for the whole clip, so colour cannot be tracking speaker identity here - it encodes speech (white) versus editor action-annotation (red), which matches the single-speaker sibling rather than the 2+ speaker ones.
